chapter: Life on the road and in the Webb band's book
title: Reeds and how he shaved them
summary: McRae used strength four and a half or five, shaved the length, and favored King reeds.

story.theme_name: The reed and horn player's craft: clarinet, sax, tone
story.community_name: Reeds, mouthpieces and horns: the reed player's gear

blocks.x: Can I ask you a trade secret now that you don't play the saxophone much anymore?
I used a five, four and a half. I used to use a five. I used to shape them

The length. Shave it down a little bit, so I can punch it more without breaking the tip, you know.
I'll shave it down and, you know, like going towards the front of the reed, you know. Take it towards the back just so it wouldn't --
Sometimes reeds go through the machine, they're not the same, you know, thickness. You have to shave them down a little bit.

Vido Musso -- I had some -- You know that reed with the -- what do you call that reed with the hole in it? What do you call that reed? It's got the stripes in the back. Had the little grooves in them.
King reeds, I think. Aren't they?
King reeds, yeah. They're good reeds. Had little grooves in the back.
